newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries firmer in London, cost data key.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries firmer in London, cost data key.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries recovered in London on Tuesday after a bout of mild selling pressure early in the session, led by European flows.

The market was apprehensive ahead of the first salvo of U.S. data in an action-packed week -- the employment cost index (ECI). The third quarter ECI, due at 1330 GMT, is forecast to rise 0.8 percent, according to a Reuters survey.
The U.S. long bond at 1051 GMT was at 98-29, up from the 98-26 closing bid in Tokyo and the 98-28 bid in New York on Monday.

Charles Quigley, vice-president at Chase in London, said Treasuries came under pressure early in Europe in line with Bunds, which fell after a German institutes report forecasting interest rates may rise and that Germany may miss a deficit target under the Maastricht Treaty. "That triggered a sell-off in Bunds, and simultaneously a push in the mark versus the dollar, triggering a number of stops and temporarily pushing dollar/mark below 1.51," he said.

"With that backdrop Treasuries began to sell off. But underneath there were some fairly strong bids. People with a somewhat longer view than the next six hours proved to be better buyers," Quigley said.
He said the the front end of the yield curve, particularly three-year paper, was performing well and supporting the market.

But he said the market was nervous about the employment index, which has only recently become a first-tier figure in the market's mind. "Six month's ago, nobody would talk about this number," he said.
The index, which measures wages and other costs to employers, gives an indication of inflationary pressures building in the economy so the market has begun to fix its attention on it.

"We think it will again say inflation is alive and well as far as the cost and wage side is concerned," said Jane Edwards, economist at Lehman Brothers in London. "The issue is: Why isn't it coming through?"
An increase of 0.8 percent would be consistent with inflation around three percent, Edwards said. "At the moment it is at a level which is not worrying."
But if the data showed a rise of one percent or more, that would give a knock to the Treasuries market, she said.
The cost index figures will be followed by consumer confidence numbers at 1500 GMT, but economists said these numbers had less potential to shake the market.
The October confidence index is forecast at 110.6, down from 111.8 in the prior month.
December U.S. T-bond futures were at 110-27, down from 110-29 at the prior close in Chicago.
